verses.1: And Jehovah gathered together the people of Israel. He defeated David in battle, saying, “You shall bring the Israelites and the Jews under your control.”
verses.2: And the king said to Joab, the chief officer, “You shall go throughout all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beer Sheva, and you shall count the people. I know the number of the people.”
verses.3: And Joshua said to the king, “May the LORD your God speak to the people in this way. Do this a hundred times over. The eyes of the king’s servants saw this. What does the king want from this?”
verses.4: And the king’s words were heard by Joab and the officers of the army. Joab and the officers of the army went before the king to rule over the people, over Israel.
verses.5: They crossed the Jordan River, and they stopped at a village on the right side of the city, which was located along the Gad River. Then they went to Ya’zar.
verses.6: And the Giladites came into the new lands below. Danaya also came, along with those around him.
verses.7: And they came from the cities of Syria and all the cities of Judah and Canaan. They went out to Mount Zion in the land of Seba.
verses.8: And they spread out over all the land. They arrived in Jerusalem after seven days and twenty days.
verses.9: Joab gave the number of men who were under his command to the king. Thus, Israel had ten thousand men in total. And each tribe of Judah had five thousand men.
verses.10: And David’s heart was moved by this. Then he wrote down the sins of the people. David said to the LORD, “I have sinned greatly in doing these things. Now, LORD, please forgive the sins of Your servant, for I have sinned greatly.”
verses.11: And David rose in the morning. And the word of the LORD was given to the prophet Zechariah. David said, “…”
verses.12: Go, and say to David, “As the LORD says, I will take one of them for myself, and I will do what I want with him.”
verses.13: And he went to David and said to him, “May seven years of famine come upon you in your land. If three days pass by before you can face your enemies again, then he will pursue you. And if three days pass by, and there is still no news from your land, then know that I, the Lord, will send disaster upon you.”
verses.14: And David said to Gad: “May it fall into the hands of Jehovah, for His mercy is great. But do not let it fall into the hands of man.”
verses.15: And the LORD brought forth a message among Israel, from morning until evening. From Dan to Beersheba, seventy thousand men died.
verses.16: And the angel stretched out his hand to destroy Jerusalem. But Jehovah would not allow this to happen. He said to the angel who was about to destroy the people: “Now, stretch out your hand!” And the angel of Jehovah was with Goren Ha’Arvna.
verses.17: And David said to the LORD, “See, I have sinned; I have done wrong. These sheep were taken from me. Please have mercy on me and on my father’s house.”
verses.18: And on that day, God came to David and said to him, “Get up and offer sacrifices to the LORD in the garden of Ebron.”
verses.19: And David obeyed God’s command, as Jehovah had commanded him.
verses.20: And Arvana saw the king and his servants walking past him. Then Arvana went forward and bowed to the king, with his head down.
verses.21: And Arvna said, “I don’t know why the king has come to me. David said that he wanted to buy from you the golden altar for the worship of God. And so, the plague will be stopped from spreading among the people.”
verses.22: And Aruna said to David, “Take and go up to the king’s palace. Look for those who are good in his eyes. Seek out those who are noble and honorable.”
verses.23: All these things were given by Arvna, the king, to the king. And Arvna said to the king, “Yahweh, your God, desires this.”
verses.24: And the king said to Aruna, “I will not buy them from your hands at a fair price. I will not pay any price for them. David will buy them with silver and gold—fifty shekels each.”
verses.25: And there David built an altar for Yahweh. He also offered sacrifices and gifts. But Yahweh refused to bless the land of Israel. Thus, the plague was brought upon Israel.
